options.name: journal_mode
options.note: How the rollback journal is kept. OFF disables atomic commit/rollback.

options.name: synchronous
options.note: How often SQLite waits for data to reach disk.

options.name: locking_mode
options.note: EXCLUSIVE keeps the file lock after the first access, so other connections are blocked.

options.name: page_size
options.note: Must be set before the database is first written; cannot be changed once in WAL mode.

options.name: cache_size
options.note: Negative = KiB, positive = number of pages.

options.name: auto_vacuum
options.note: Must be set before the first table is created. FULL returns free pages to the OS at every commit.

options.name: temp_store
options.note: Where temporary tables and indices are kept.

options.name: foreign_keys
options.note: Foreign key constraints are enforced only when ON.

options.name: secure_delete
options.note: ON overwrites deleted content with zeros.

constraints_and_dependencies.text: page_size and auto_vacuum must be applied before any table is created (and page_size before switching to WAL); the apply script therefore sets them first on a fresh database file.
With journal_mode=OFF, ROLLBACK is not guaranteed to restore the previous state; a rollback check is not a valid oracle for this setting.
With locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE, a second connection cannot access the database while the first connection is open.
auto_vacuum=FULL leaves no free pages after a commit that deletes data; NONE keeps them on the freelist; INCREMENTAL keeps them until PRAGMA incremental_vacuum.
foreign_keys=ON rejects an insert that references a missing parent row; OFF accepts it.
